scaling.note: PHASE 2A, TYLER: "Thad looks too small next to the bar." His art is frozen, so the room changed. THE CURVE IS RESCALED BY 1.145 AND ITS SHAPE IS UNTOUCHED -- 198/459 became 227/526 on the same horizon (y 239) -- which is the median of eight dimensioned things measured off this plate at 3x and 4x (reference/room-03-candidate/furniture-measurements.json). THE READINGS DO NOT AGREE with each other: at the same depth the card table says a 222 px man and the piano says 356. That is what a painted room is, and it is why this takes a median rather than crowning one object. The three bar stools alone agree with the OLD curve; the counter and the piano do not. THE CURVE WAS NOT THE WHOLE DEFECT, and this is the part no rescale could have fixed: the walkable floor turned in at x 1170-1379 and stopped up to 440 px short of the bar's own plinth, so wherever Thad stood the counter was at a SHALLOWER depth than he was and read across his shoulders -- 0.87 of his stature, measured. Carrying the floor to the plinth puts it at 0.63, waist and lower ribs, which is where a bar belongs on a man. The study is proofs/room-03/phase2a-scale-study.json and renders/opening-set-retrofit/phase2a-nugget-scale.webp; the candidates are scale-candidates.json beside this file. STILL WRONG AND NOT FIXED: the painted piano tops him at every candidate -- it reads about 1.7 m against furniture that reads 1.75 m men. The environment is OWNER-ACCEPTED AND FROZEN, and the only fix is repainting it, so it is recorded for Tyler rather than corrected.

beyond.note: THE STOVE'S OWN BASE LINE, and this is not an extrapolation choice the way Room 1's was. This curve is a true perspective by construction: 227 at y 506 and 526 at y 858 is a straight line that reaches zero at y 239, which is the horizon this room's scaling note already names. Continuing it above the band is therefore the SAME perspective and not a second model -- 0.8494 x (412 - 239) = 147. IT IS NEEDED BECAUSE heightIn CLAMPS ABOVE farY. Tyler, 2026-09-12: the stove man reads as standing at the card table's depth and must stand at the back of the room with the stove, and his placement is staging, not a player-navigation target. Without this sample he would be drawn at 227 wherever he stood behind the band -- a man at the back of the room at the size of a man at the front of it. CROSS-CHECKED against the door behind the stove, whose panel runs y 250 to the floor at 430: 180 px for a two-metre door puts a 1.75 m man at 157 there, and the curve says 162. Six per cent, on a door measured off a painting.

occlusion.note: ONE PLANE, AND IT IS THE SPITTOON (Tyler, 2026-09-12). Phase 2A made the spittoon's OBSTACLE its base line rather than its silhouette, because the whole drawn object stood in open dirt and cut the near floor in two. That was right, and it left this: Thad may now walk BEHIND the spittoon, and with no plane cut he drew over it -- a man at y 800 with a brass spittoon at y 745-864 in front of him and his shins on top of it. The mask is a 1-bit stencil over the plate's own pixels and is never drawn, so nothing is duplicated and nothing shifts. THE BANDS BEHIND ITS BASE TAKE PLANE 1 AND THE BAND IN FRONT TAKES 0: floor_6 runs 813-864 and the brass stands on 824, so a man down there is nearer than it and is masked by nothing. Everywhere else in those bands the mask is transparent, so a man at the far end of the room is unaffected by a plane he is nominally on. NOTHING ELSE IN THIS ROOM OCCLUDES ANYBODY. The seven furniture-dependent patrons are painted into the plate and need no plane; the floor still stops at the bar's plinth, so nobody passes behind the counter; the stove man stands at 1145,508 and the nearest thing that could cross him is the card group, whose right-hand chair back ends at x 1100 while his sprite starts at 1098 -- two pixels, and he is not cut by them.

planes.note: The spittoon, authored as a polygon because it cannot be thresholded: in the band around it the brass runs luminance 19-84 against dirt at 31-51 and warmth 44-64 against 45-53, which is the same lamps lighting both. tools/retrofit/nugget-spittoon-mask.py, --check draws it back over the art.

proofPoints.note: Directly behind the spittoon and 24 px above its base. The brass stands at 745-864 and he stands at 800, so it crosses him from the knee down -- 4% of the figure, which is the whole of what a spittoon should take and is exactly what he drew straight over before this plane was cut. TWO POINTS WERE DROPPED FROM THIS LIST and the reason is worth keeping: one stood in the same band 200 px along, where the mask is transparent, and the check refuses a point claiming an occlusion its mask cannot produce; the other stood in front of the brass at plane 0, and a plane a room does not declare cannot be proved. There is in any case no walkable ground DIRECTLY in front of the spittoon -- its obstacle runs from y 824 to the frame's foot, which is phase 2A's correction and stands.

plateNote: BACKGROUND COMPOSITE CLEANUP (Tyler, 2026-09-12): the plate is rebuild-03. Both characters are owner-accepted and immovable, and the remaining faults were in the art around them. THREE REPAIRS, all deterministic raster, no image operation, ledger 47/47, tools/retrofit/nugget-plate-cleanup.py. (1) THE CARD CLUSTER PAVED ITS FLOOR and the salvage repaired it from y 505 DOWN, taking everything above for shadow under the table. Right of the group it is open lit floor and the stove man stood on it; he moved to the back of the room and the plank was the first thing you saw. Dirt restored wherever the accepted cold-dirt plate has aligned dirt to give back -- out = acceptedDirt x (shipping low-frequency / accepted low-frequency), so grain and colour are canonical and every shadow the rebuilt room added survives as the ratio. ABOVE y 510 BETWEEN x 700 AND 1080 IT DOES NOT: the accepted plate stands its own card table and four chairs on exactly those coordinates, so there is no source, that band is left, and at gameplay tone it is shadow under a table. (2) THE BAR'S FAR END. The endpoint's run stops being furniture nine pixels early -- a counter top ending at x 1185, a front face at x 1191, and between them a flat untextured smear with no top, no plinth and no contact with the floor. A first draft restored the ACCEPTED plate's end panel, which is the one thing this pass must not do: that bar ends 22 px further right and restoring it shortens the current run. The end is built from the CURRENT bar's own front face, the slice at x 1196-1203 moved 11 px left and 3 up on the run's own measured slope and darkened to 0.72 for an end turned away from the lamp. (3) THE PLATFORM UNDER THE FOREGROUND PATRON IS THE TRANSLATION'S SLACK. The grounding composites the whole plate shifted 82 rows inside his shifted outline, and that outline is deliberately loose. Below his old outline's bottom at y 711 the slack covers FLOOR, and there the shifted plate laid the bar's kick-board, plinth and rail on the dirt behind his boots. The floor is given back from rebuild-01 -- the same room, the same rebuilt bar, unshifted -- outside an authored mask of his two boots, and the grounding's contact shadows are re-applied over it. HE DOES NOT MOVE BY ONE PIXEL AND NOT ONE PIXEL OF HIM IS REPAINTED. THE LESSON IS ENFORCED, not just written down: art/staging/room-03/cluster-integrations.json lists every cluster, its WHOLE footprint and what it imported, and tools/check-cluster-floor.mjs fails if any floor pixel of any footprint is unrepaired and unwritten-off, or if the plate changes under a clearance. ROOM 3 REBUILD (Tyler, 2026-09-11). THE PLATE IS NO LONGER PEOPLE-FREE. Tyler accepted the build decision and ruled that the seven furniture-dependent patrons -- four card players and three bar men -- ship as STATIC STAGING baked into the background, with their LOOK and LISTEN copy on the room hotspots, and that only the landing man and the stove man stay runtime actors. That is the method the ORIGINAL shipping Nugget used: art/backgrounds/room-03-nugget.png drew its seated men in the same pass as its furniture. Two sources. The salvaged card cluster, blitted back at the integer x2 it was composed at with its plank floor replaced by this room's own dirt (tools/retrofit/nugget-card-salvage.py). And the ONE authorized bar operation, taken from plate x 1176 rightward (tools/retrofit/nugget-bar-integrate.py). PHASE 1.5C (doc 36 Q119, owner review of 1.5B failed): the accepted clean plate with ONE continuous dirt floor across the whole public floor -- the third and final floor operation, the whole floor under a mask with no furniture holes and no rectangular restore; the model's floor stands under and between every leg, the model's furniture stands as it kept it, and only the spittoon's tight brass silhouette comes back from the accepted plate. Stove out in the base, fire in the lit overlay, unchanged. art/staging/room-03/corrected-03/derivation.json.

population.note: ROOM 3 REBUILD (Tyler, 2026-09-11). THE NUGGET'S POPULATION IS NINE AND SEVEN OF THEM ARE PAINT. The owner ruled the four card players and the three bar men into the background art as static staging, keeping only the landing man and the stove man as runtime actors, and the count therefore stopped being something a test could get by counting ambient files.
